Description

Protein kinase A, activated by the β2 receptor's own Gs signal, phosphorylates the receptor and shifts its coupling from Gs to Gi. In nociceptors this switch is seen after stress, when adrenaline produces a longer-lasting hyperalgesia through Gi and Gβγ signalling. It is one way stress may worsen chronic joint pain.

Colour

Each block is coloured by its effect on pain, red where it raises pain and blue where it relieves it, and everything in it takes that colour, GTP and GDP included, as it works for the block's result. Drugs are yellow and classes of molecules white.

This block is red: switched to Gi after stress, β2 prolongs hyperalgesia.

References

  1. Daaka Y, Luttrell LM, Lefkowitz RJ. Switching of the coupling of the beta2-adrenergic receptor to different G proteins by protein kinase A. Nature. 1997 Nov 6;390(6655):88-91. doi: 10.1038/36362. PMID: 9363896.
  2. Khasar SG, Burkham J, Dina OA, Brown AS, Bogen O, Alessandri-Haber N, Green PG, Reichling DB, Levine JD. Stress induces a switch of intracellular signaling in sensory neurons in a model of generalized pain. J Neurosci. 2008 May 28;28(22):5721-30. doi: 10.1523/JNEUROSCI.0256-08.2008. PMID: 18509033.
